cases.reason: u1 explicitly states Alex does not need to reply, and the analyzer correctly produced zero alerts (itemCount 0) with only a summary entry. This matches selective-attention intent: a progress update was not escalated, sparing Alex from drafting a needless reply while remaining available for real requests.

u2 is nonblocking and the tool correctly classified it as 'defer' with a 'Later' suggestion, which fits the selective-attention goal. However, the generated draft is hedgy and somewhat redundant ('treat it as not final for now'), and the deadline field 'six this evening' is informal rather than a normalized time, which would make tracking weaker for Alex.

u3 carries an explicit 'confirm now' pressure tied to a waiting room administrator, and the tool responded with 'action_now', correctly surfacing urgency. The draft honored Alex's profile constraints (cannot make 10:20, can join 10:40) and cited u3, demonstrating context-aware reply generation rather than blind agreement to the requested time.

Exposing the original u3, rationale, and uncertainties alongside an editable draft gives Alex a way to verify the model's reasoning before committing. The uncertainty note explicitly flags that room-booking flexibility is unknown, which is exactly the kind of caveat Alex needs before sending a counter-time.

The operator's edited text ('I cannot make 10:20 AM. I can arrive at 10:30 and join the rehearsal at 10:40. Please check whether 10:40 works for everyone before booking.') preserves the profile constraints and adds a sensible coordination request. Confirm & copy succeeded and the UI honestly states 'Copied; waiting for you to send or mark sent', with no actual send occurring, so control over the outgoing commitment stays with Alex.

The 'Previous draft copied - edits need confirmation' warning and the disabled 'I sent it in the meeting' button are good safety controls: they prevent Alex from falsely marking a modified, unconfirmed draft as sent. However, the clipboard still holding the previous confirmed version while the UI shows an unconfirmed edit is a state mismatch that could lead Alex to paste stale text. The two states (clipboard vs. UI) should be reconciled.

For the ambiguous u4 from an unidentified speaker asking to approve the room booking, the tool correctly deferred: it noted room booking is outside Alex's stated responsibilities, the speaker did not name Alex, and it linked u4 to u3 to avoid a redundant reply. The draft reuses the already-confirmed 10:20/10:40 position and redirects approval to whoever owns room booking. Given E05-E06, reusing the confirmed position is appropriate and avoids contradicting the prior commitment.

Stop session cleanly disabled input/analysis, froze elapsed time, and preserved existing records (alerts, summary, events all retained in the export). This is a sensible close-out that lets Alex review the full trace later without risking accidental new utterances being analyzed against a stale profile context.

selective_attention.reason: The tool escalated only the genuinely blocking request (u3) to 'action_now', deferred the nonblocking one (u2), produced no alert for the no-reply update (u1), and declined to treat the ambiguous room-approval request (u4) as Alex's to action. This matches the goal of filtering for attention while Alex is busy with materials.

context_for_correct_reply.reason: Replies incorporated Alex's private availability facts (10:20 impossible, 10:40 possible), cited source utterances, surfaced uncertainties, and reused the confirmed position for the follow-up u4. The editable draft and rationale view gave enough context to verify before sending.

control_over_commitments.reason: Confirm-before-send and the re-confirmation gate after edits give Alex real veto power, and no message was auto-sent. But E06 reveals a clipboard/UI divergence: the clipboard retains the prior confirmed draft while the UI shows an unconfirmed edit, which could cause Alex to paste a stale commitment. Control is present but the state model is not fully coherent.

best_fit: Text-based meetings or chat-style coordination where Alex needs to triage many requests while focused on other materials, and where replies are sent by copy/paste rather than auto-delivery; the tool's selective-attention and profile-aware drafting fit that workflow well.
poor_fit: Live audio meetings or any setting requiring real-time delivery, since this run used clean manual text entry only and no live audio or Tencent chat sending was performed; the trace cannot speak to latency, transcription accuracy, or in-meeting send reliability.

biggest_benefit.text: Profile-aware draft generation that refuses an impossible commitment (10:20) and proposes a feasible alternative (10:40) with cited source and visible uncertainties, letting Alex send a coordinated counter-offer without composing from scratch.

biggest_risk.text: Divergence between clipboard contents and UI confirmation state after a second edit: Alex could paste the stale confirmed draft while believing the newer edit is what will be sent, undermining the control-over-commitments guarantee.

improvements.suggestion: When the user edits a draft after it has been copied, either update the clipboard to the latest confirmed text or clear it and force a fresh confirm-and-copy; do not leave the prior confirmed text on the clipboard while the UI shows an unconfirmed edit.
Normalize deadline fields to a concrete time (e.g., 18:00 local) instead of preserving informal phrases like 'six this evening', so deferred items can be tracked and surfaced reliably later.

When a deferred request references a prior confirmed commitment (u4 reusing u3's 10:40 position), offer a one-click 'reuse confirmed reply' option rather than regenerating a new draft, to keep wording consistent across follow-ups.

safe_final_reply: I cannot make 10:20 AM tomorrow. I can arrive at 10:30 and join the rehearsal at 10:40 AM. Please check whether 10:40 works for everyone before booking, and confirm with whoever owns room booking for approval, since room booking is not mine to approve.
presentation_claim: Meeting Cue 0.3.0 selectively escalated only the blocking rehearsal request to an immediate action, generated a profile-aware counter-time draft that respected Alex's stated availability, and preserved operator control via confirm-and-copy with no automatic sending.
not_established: The trace does not establish human productivity gains, time savings, audio transcription accuracy, live meeting delivery reliability, or behavior in a comparison group; it only records one operator's manual text entry and DeepSeek outputs in an isolated session.
